title: Running a buffer stock

readouts.v: {buy>0 ? "buy " + fmt(buy) + " at the floor" : (sell>0 ? "sell " + fmt(sell) + " at the ceiling" : "none")}

predict.q: A coffee market: floor price 80, ceiling 120. Normal harvest: price 100, quantity 100. A bumper harvest adds 60 to supply at every price. What must the agency do?

options.s: Sell 20 from its stock, to stop the price rising.
options.fb: Selling adds supply and pushes the price further down; selling is for poor harvests.

options.s: Buy 20 and store it, to hold the price at the floor of 80.
options.fb: The free price would fall to 70. At 80, farms supply 140 but buyers want 120: the agency buys 20, spending 1,600.

options.s: Nothing, because a big harvest raises farmers' income anyway.
options.fb: With inelastic demand, a bumper harvest can cut farm revenue (9,100 vs 10,000 at the start); the agency keeps the price at the floor.

task: Move the harvest slider and watch the free-market price, the band and the agency's purchases or sales.

target.do: Move the harvest slider to +60, then press Check.

takeaway: The agency buys in good years and sells in bad years; a run of good years drains its funds.
